name: 265. Passthrough tuning is refused for virtual keys and method overrides never reach the provider (passthrough-tuning-vk) [SERIAL]
description: TXE-5023 (PR5 H12 port). Bifrost forwards a passthrough request under the shared provider key, and no provider records which key created a tuning job or tuned model, so a tenant's virtual key could list every job on the shared OpenAI key and cancel another tenant's. With client.enforce_vk_object_ownership on (the default), a virtual-key passthrough request that reaches a tuning or customization collection (OpenAI fine_tuning and ft: models, Gemini tunedModels, Vertex tuningJobs, Bedrock's customization collections) is refused with 403 by governance before any provider call, whatever the method or the path spelling and whichever passthrough route carries it. A method-override header (X-HTTP-Method-Override and its variants) is never forwarded, directly or through x-bf-eh-*, because governance judges a request by its method. Inference through passthrough is unchanged. Red before the change: the list and cancel reached the provider, and an override header reached it too. The refusals never reach a provider; the override cases send an upload without a file, which the provider rejects; the chat case spends a few tokens on gpt-4o-mini. The virtual keys are created and deleted by the folder. The Gemini rows check that inference on a tuned model stays open to a key allowing that model by name, while reading, deleting or transferring it, or a path that only resembles inference, is refused; they need an offline stub serving a tuned model and run only when passthroughTuningStub=1 is set, so the live sweep skips them.

pm.test('passthrough-tuning-vk: virtual key created', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code, 'failed: ' + pm.response.text()).to.be.oneOf([200, 201]); });
